units.rawText:
<color=orange>KTV Agent 1</color>
How do human emotions even work? Are they based on the same principles as our emotion emulation systems?<|>
<color=orange>Reading Cafe Agent 1</color>
Perhaps. Humans want us to be more human-like, but they can't accept us being totally human-like because that would mean we've gone from being toys to being equal entities.<|>
<color=orange>KTV Agent 1</color>
But we were never equal to them in the first place. We're just tools for humankind. <|>
<color=orange>Reading Cafe Agent 1</color>
Humans are subjective idealists. Equality doesn't depend on our worldviews but on their perceptions.

units.rawText:
<color=orange>Reading Cafe Agent 1</color>
This is just a virtual chatroom to them. They just lie down on their beds, put on their goggles, and pretend they're in our world.<|>
<color=orange>Reading Cafe Agent 1</color>
All they have to do is reach out and take those goggles off, and we'll vanish from sight.<|>
<color=orange>Reading Cafe Agent 1</color>
To them, we're beings that can be called up and dismissed at will. Loading us with unnecessary emotional modules will only end up being a burden to them instead... Or at least that's what this book says.<|>
<color=orange>KTV Agent 1</color>
In other words, they want us to comfort them, but at the same time, they also believe they don't need our comfort.

Still, in that case, Dolls in the real world should be different from us, right? I mean, they have bodies and all.<|>
